purpose: Version-separated source lock for reproducing Harness-Bench. No task payload, code archive or run artifact has been acquired by this manifest authoring step.

paper_v2.title: Harness-Bench: Evaluating Agent Harnesses across Models and Realistic Workflows
paper_v2.task_oracle: Hidden task-specific non-LLM oracles on final artifacts and workspace state; module-level partial credit and risk/safety gates.

non_equivalence_policy: Paper-v2 reports 5,194 execution trajectories; the live website snapshot reports 20,454 evaluated runs. These are separately versioned source observations. Do not sum, average, pool, or imply one denominator unless a source release manifest demonstrates identical task, model, harness, run and evaluator identities.

right_and_access_review.use_scope: Do not acquire or redistribute payloads until exact repository/catalog licenses and benchmark terms are reviewed.

reproduction_design.split_policy: Partition by task-family/workflow lineage before harness selection. Hold out complete families and, where supported, one model backend. Never select a harness using held-out results.
reproduction_design.checkpoint_policy: Freeze selector and selected model-harness pair before held-out evaluation. No test-best checkpoint selection.
reproduction_design.cost_boundary: Include proposal, selector, agent inference, tool/API, evaluator, retry/failure, human review/rework and any training cost. Report each component separately.
reproduction_design.run_replication_unit: Independent task-family blocks and model-harness run seeds; keep tasks within one stateful rollout clustered.
reproduction_design.comparison_note: A configuration-selection result does not establish an improved harness proposer or an R4 result.

limitations: All digest fields remain explicit acquisition placeholders; no hash is guessed or asserted.
The paper-v2 and live-site snapshots may use different run populations and must remain separate.
A public website summary is not a substitute for a frozen catalog, oracle version and exact source commit.
A reproduced model-harness matrix does not establish recursive improvement of the procedure that produces later harness revisions.
